notes: Determines whether the new guard's grandfathering clause is correctly scoped. RESOLVED FALSE: one of the 12 parseable JSONs already records a checkpoint hash -- hound_track_desert_s0_deterministic_vs_stochastic.json carries checkpoint_sha256_16 = a30726fe3e0e602b, an ad-hoc TRUNCATED 16-char field under a non-standard name, and it is a correct prefix of the full a30726fe3e0e602b5feada0ae16a3ea4e25482e288b2417031d41d34d40f4e9b in the hound_track_desert_s0_final_checkpoints.sha256 sidecar. 9 of 12 name a checkpoint; 8 of those record no hash at all. Being wrong here changed the build: the guard now also asserts a truncated hash agrees with the full one in the same file, which it would not have done if the prediction had held.  AMBIGUITY, stated rather than resolved quietly: the claim names the FIELD 'checkpoint_sha256', and no file records a field by that name -- read literally it is TRUE. It is graded FALSE on the reading the claim was written to test ('does the record already carry checkpoint identity'), because it does, under another name. The defect is in the prediction, which conflated a field name with a concept; a claim that can be graded either way by choosing a reading is not falsifiable, and picking the reading after seeing the answer is the exact failure calibration exists to prevent. Future claims name the concept and give the field as an example, not the reverse.
